theme: Order jobs on a one-way multi-station line
title: One-Way Conveyor: Warm-Up Windows vs. Tool Fatigue
strategies: trivial: keep the as-given arrival order untouched (the evaluator's own baseline construction) -> exactly 0.1

greedy: classic shortest-processing-time (SPT) sort by each job's own proc_time, ignoring the shared multi-station setup/warm-up and fatigue state entirely -- the trap: proc_time is not always a safe proxy for type, and even where it is, SPT's resulting long same-type runs can blow a station's fatigue limit it never modeled

strong: build several candidate sequences across a spread of block granularities C using two chunking schemes (round-robin across all types, and majority-first with single-job breather resets), self-score every candidate with the exact public multi-station cost model, keep the true best, then polish with adjacent-swap hill-climbing -- treats block granularity as the decision variable that jointly trades off cross-station warm-up transient against fatigue overrun, since one shared permutation commits every station's tooling state at once
invalid: repeats job 0 for every slot -- not a permutation -> infeasible -> 0
